newsitem.title: UK: Analysts grow restless awaiting C&W alliance.
newsitem.headline: Analysts grow restless awaiting C&W alliance.

text.p: Telecoms analysts said on Wednesday they were growing restless at a failure of Cable and Wireless Plc to form a partnership with Global One, adding that the alliance may be distancing itself from the British group.

At an analyst meeting, C&W's chief executive Richard Brown focused on the firm's strategy to sink its roots deeper into markets -- but analysts were disappointed that he alluded to Vietnam, Panama, Bulgaria and Latvia rather than key markets such as France, Germany and the U.S. which would make more money for C&W shareholders.
"If you are going to be a global player, it is much more important to get Germany and France right than to get Latvia and Bulgaria right," noted one analyst, who declined to be named.
C&W abandoned its German alliance with VEBA AG in February because it said it wanted to concentrate on its new cable venture, Cable and Wireless Communications, which it was launching in Britain.

The analyst also said that comments made on Tuesday by the chairman of Deutsche Telekom AG, who leads the Global One partnership with France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp, indicated that no imminent deal was on the cards.

"A deal with Global One would be an acceptable way out, but it's not clear that they can -- or that there is indeed an offer on the table from the Global One partners for C&W to do a deal with," the analyst noted.
"The meeting wasn't disastrous but none of it was very convincing and I think that nothing more than that is why the shares are being marked off today," he added.
By 1100 GMT, C&W's shares had fallen 15.5p to 497p.
Some analysts say now is the time for C&W, whose main assets are limited to Britian and Hong Kong, to accept a humble role as a junior partner in someone else's global alliance.
Andrew Harrington at Salomon Brothers took heart from Brown's comments that the company was continuing to talk to a number of potential partners in global alliances but had made no decision yet.
"This reinforces the view that I've taken, which is that these guys are the pretty girl at the ball whom everybody wants to talk to. Sooner or later they'll decide who to dance with," he said.
Global One lacks access to both Britain and Asia.

He noted that annual pre-tax profits, which came in at 1.42 billion stg after exceptional items, were at the top half of the range of expectations at an underlying level and said the company deserved credit for a good performance from its British telecoms subsidiary Mercury.
Stripping out exceptional items, pre-tax profits rose around 4.5 percent to 1.317 billion stg, analysts said.
C&W said its operating margin, which shows the company's ability to control costs and increase revenues, improved to 25 percent from 24 percent.
